newsitem.title: ITALY: Ex-head of Italy's Finmeccanica to stand trial.
newsitem.headline: Ex-head of Italy's Finmeccanica to stand trial.

text.p: The former head of Italian state engineering company Finmeccanica, Fabiano Fabiani, was charged with balance sheet fraud and abuse of office on Thursday and ordered to stand trial.
Fabiani resigned as chairman in April after the group's parent company, state holding Iri, ordered him to reverse his strategy of bringing the Finmeccanica empire under one umbrella.

An appeal court in Rome ruled that Fabiani should go on trial to answer charges that the company paid out more than four trillion lire ($2.4 million) to consultants for non-existent services between 1986 and 1993, when he was managing director.
No date for the trial was set.
Fabiani's lawyer, Giuseppe De Luca, called the ruling surprising. He said in a statement that no fraud was involved and that the consultancy fees had been accounted for regularly.
Finmeccanica's interests range from weapons production to space technology and engineering plant. Much of its business is conducted in the Third World.
Thursday's ruling overturned a lower court decision taken two years ago not to proceed against Fabiani in the case.
The judges, however, upheld the lower court's decision to drop proceedings against 14 other people involved in the case, including two former Italian ambassadors and an ex-admiral.
